name: Onlysans
classification_notes: Post-geometric in that it builds on a strict grid and geometric principles but introduces deliberate irregularities and mischievous details. Duplexed – all letters maintain identical advance widths across every weight – which echoes rationalist sans traditions while consciously rejecting timelessness as a design goal.
summary: A duplexed post-geometric sans that pairs disciplined grid-work with deliberately mischievous details.
description: Onlysans maintains identical letter widths across all weights – a property called duplexing – giving it an unusual rhythmic consistency regardless of weight. Its forms appear clean and grid-based yet carry playful alternates, contrasting corner treatments and a conscious refusal to be timeless. Well suited to branding and interface work where precision and light eccentricity need to coexist.
foundry_blurb: Daria Cohen describes Onlysans as a post-geometric sans that looks rational, clean and modern but hides strange mischievous details. Because it is duplexed, letters occupy the same space at every weight – a futile attempt at stability, she says. It was designed for branding, interfaces and projects that call for strange precision with a touch of entropy, and is explicitly not meant to be timeless.

name: Superfluous
classification_notes: A hand-drawn upright script drawing on Pennsylvania Dutch folk lettering traditions. Lacks the formal flow of calligraphic scripts; the letterforms are deliberately imperfect and festive, positioned closer to vernacular lettering than to brush or chancery traditions.
summary: A slow, festive naive script drawing on Pennsylvania Dutch folk lettering with a randomiser stylistic set.
description: Superfluous is a hand-drawn script that sits somewhere between Pennsylvania Dutch birth certificate lettering and a handwritten postcard – intentionally naive rather than polished. It includes three OpenType stylistic sets: one that randomises capitalisation for an organic all-caps mode, and two catering to small caps usage. A limited but characterful choice for seasonal, festive or folk-inflected design work.
foundry_blurb: Daria Cohen describes Superfluous as a slow, festive and naive script – somewhere between Pennsylvania Dutch birth certificates and her best effort at writing a heartfelt postcard. It does not try to imitate skillful calligraphy; it just tries to be nice, real hard. Some features are, by the designer's own admission, superfluous.
